title: Code of the District of Columbia, Title 34 (Public Utilities), Chapter 11 - Service, Valuation, Accounts
verified_how: fetched https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/titles/34/chapters/11: breadcrumb 'Title 34. Public Utilities. / Chapter 11. Service, Valuation, Accounts.' and the full section list, opening 's 34-1101. Utility service and charges to be just and reasonable; certification required.' and including 's 34-1120. Commission to fix adequate and serviceable standards; regulations for testing products, service, and meters.', 's 34-1123. Schedule of rates to be filed; existing rates to remain in force until changed.' and 's 34-1129. Utility not to receive greater or less compensation than fixed in schedule.' Only s 34-1104 is marked '[Repealed]'. Not marked '[Repealed]' or '[Not Funded]' (the register marks both inline, e.g. 'Chapter 5A. Freedom to Contract Within the Broadcast Industry. [Repealed]' in the same title). Currency: the Code's Publication Information block reads 'Current through Sept. 5, 2026', 'Last codified D.C. Law: Law 26-177 effective Sept. 5, 2026', 'Last codified Emergency Law: Act 26-416 effective Aug. 13, 2026', 'Last codified Federal Law: Public Law 115-334 approved Dec. 20, 2018'.
notes: Chosen over the neighbouring chapters because this is where the customer-facing duties sit: charges must be just and reasonable, only the filed schedule may be billed, and meters and service standards are regulated. Adjacent chapters seen on the same Title 34 list and deliberately not chosen: ch. 9 Rates, Examinations, Investigations, and Hearings (ss 34-901 - 34-922, the rate-case procedure), ch. 4A Community Residential Facilities Third-Party Notice of Utility Disconnection (ss 34-411.01 - 34-411.06), ch. 15 Retail Electric Competition and Consumer Protection (ss 34-1501 - 34-1522) and ch. 16C Retail Natural Gas Supplier Licensing and Consumer Protection (ss 34-1671.01 - 34-1671.14). Much of the day-to-day billing and disconnection detail is in PSC regulation (15 DCMR), not statute.
